It is given by -\n\n        E(u) = Integral (-inf to u) [ (x^k)*pdf(x) dx ] + (u^k)(1-cdf(u))\n\n        where, pdf is the probability density function and cdf is the\n        cumulative density function of the distribution.\n\n        Reference\n        ---------\n        Klugman, S. {"prompt": "def parse_request(cls, sock):\n    \"\"\"Parse the request (the pre-execution) section of the nailgun protocol from the given socket.\n\n    Handles reading of the Argument, Environment, Working Directory and Command chunks from the\n    client which represents the \"request\" phase of the exchange. Working Directory and Command are\n    required and must be sent as the last two chunks in this phase. Argument and Environment chunks\n    are optional and can be sent more than once (thus we aggregate them).\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    # Read the first chunk (the argument chunk)\n    arg_chunk = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n    if arg_chunk is None:\n        return None\n\n    # Read the environment chunk\n    env_chunk = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n    if env_chunk is None:\n        return None\n\n    # Read the working directory chunk\n    cwd_chunk = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n    if cwd_chunk is None:\n        return None\n\n    # Read the command chunk\n    cmd_chunk = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n    if cmd_chunk is None:\n        return None\n\n    # Read the remaining chunks (if any)\n    chunks = []\n    while True:\n        chunk = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n        if chunk is None:\n            break\n        chunks.append(chunk)\n\n    # Return the parsed request\n    return cls(arg_chunk, env_chunk, cwd_chunk, cmd_chunk, chunks)\n\n\nclass Response(object):\n    \"\"\"Represents a response to a request from the client.\n\n    The response is sent back to the client after the execution of the command.\n    \"\"\"\n    def", "solution": "\n\n    command = None\n    working_dir = None\n    arguments = []\n    environment = {}\n\n    while not all((working_dir, command)):\n      chunk_type, payload = cls.read_chunk(sock)\n\n      if chunk_type == ChunkType.ARGUMENT:\n        arguments.append(payload)\n      elif chunk_type == ChunkType.ENVIRONMENT:\n        key, val = payload.split(cls.ENVIRON_SEP, 1)\n        environment[key] = val\n      elif chunk_type == ChunkType.WORKING_DIR:\n        working_dir = payload\n      elif chunk_type == ChunkType.COMMAND:\n        command = payload\n      else:\n        raise cls.ProtocolError('received non-request chunk before header was fully received!')\n\n    return working_dir, command, arguments, environment"}

Reversibility is not assumed.\n\n    Remark\n    ------\n    Note, that this function uses a different normalization convention for the sensitivity compared to\n    eigenvector_sensitivity. See there for further information.\n    \"\"\"", "output": "envector sensitivity.\n\n    \"\"\"\n    n = T.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for i in range(n):\n        x[i, j] = 1.0 - T[i, j]\n    return x\n\n\ndef", "solution": "\n\n    n = len(T)\n\n    lEV = numpy.ones(n)\n    rEV = stationary_distribution(T)\n    eVal = 1.0\n\n    T = numpy.transpose(T)\n\n    vecA = numpy.zeros(n)\n    vecA[j] = 1.0\n\n    matA = T - eVal * numpy.identity(n)\n    # normalize s.t. sum is one using rEV which is constant\n    matA = numpy.concatenate((matA, [lEV]))\n\n    phi = numpy.linalg.lstsq(numpy.transpose(matA), vecA, rcond=-1)\n    phi = numpy.delete(phi[0], -1)\n\n    sensitivity = -numpy.outer(rEV, phi) + numpy.dot(phi, rEV) * numpy.outer(rEV, lEV)\n\n    return sensitivity"}

{"prompt": "def convex_hull(points):\n    \"\"\"Computes the convex hull of an iterable of (x, y) coordinates.\n\n    Args:\n        points: iterable of (x, y) tuples.\n\n    Returns:\n        `list`: instances of `Point` - vertices of the convex hull in\n        counter-clockwise order, starting from the vertex with the\n        lexicographically smallest coordinates.\n\n    Andrew's monotone chain algorithm. O(n log n) complexity.\n    https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Algorithm_Implementation/Geometry/Convex_hull/Monotone_chain\n    \"\"\"", "output": " \"\"\"\n    points = sorted(points)\n\n    def", "solution": "\n\n    def is_not_clockwise(p0, p1, p2):\n        return 0 <= (\n            (p1[0] - p0[0]) * (p2[1] - p0[1]) -\n            (p1[1] - p0[1]) * (p2[0] - p0[0])\n        )\n\n    def go(points_):\n        res = []\n        for p in points_:\n            while 1 < len(res) and is_not_clockwise(res[-2], res[-1], p):\n                res.pop()\n            res.append(p)\n\n        # The last point in each list is the first point in the other list\n        res.pop()\n\n        return res\n\n    # Discard duplicates and sort by x then y\n    points = sorted(set(points))\n\n    # Algorithm needs at least two points\n    hull = (\n        points if len(points) < 2 else chain(go(points), go(reversed(points)))\n    )\n\n    return list(map(Point._make, hull))"}

{"prompt": "def funcHrf(varNumVol, varTr):\n    \"\"\"Create double gamma function.\n\n    Source:\n    http://www.jarrodmillman.com/rcsds/lectures/convolution_background.html\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    return (varNumVol * (varTr / 2.0)) / (1.0 + varNumVol * (varTr / 2.0))\n\n\ndef", "solution": "\n    vecX = np.arange(0, varNumVol, 1)\n\n    # Expected time of peak of HRF [s]:\n    varHrfPeak = 6.0 / varTr\n    # Expected time of undershoot of HRF [s]:\n    varHrfUndr = 12.0 / varTr\n    # Scaling factor undershoot (relative to peak):\n    varSclUndr = 0.35\n\n    # Gamma pdf for the peak\n    vecHrfPeak = gamma.pdf(vecX, varHrfPeak)\n    # Gamma pdf for the undershoot\n    vecHrfUndr = gamma.pdf(vecX, varHrfUndr)\n    # Combine them\n    vecHrf = vecHrfPeak - varSclUndr * vecHrfUndr\n\n    # Scale maximum of HRF to 1.0:\n    vecHrf = np.divide(vecHrf, np.max(vecHrf))\n\n    return vecHrf"}

{"prompt": "def _build_likelihood(self):\n        \"\"\"\n        Construct a tensorflow function to compute the bound on the marginal\n        likelihood.\n        \"\"\"", "output": "\n        # The likelihood is the product of the likelihoods of each data point.\n        # We compute the log likelihoods, and then sum them.\n        log_likelihoods = []\n        for i in range(self.num_data_points):\n            log_likelihoods.append(self._build_likelihood_for_data_point(i))\n        log_likelihood = tf.add_n(log_likelihoods)\n\n        # We compute the bound on the marginal likelihood by adding the\n        # log likelihood to the log prior.\n        log_prior = self._build_log_prior()\n        log_likelihood_bound = log_likelihood + log_prior\n\n        # We compute the bound on the marginal likelihood by adding the\n        # log likelihood to the log prior.\n        log_likelihood_bound = log_likelihood + log_prior\n\n        # We return the bound on the marginal likelihood.\n        return log_likelihood_bound\n\n    def", "solution": "\n        pX = DiagonalGaussian(self.X_mean, self.X_var)\n\n        num_inducing = len(self.feature)\n        psi0 = tf.reduce_sum(expectation(pX, self.kern))\n        psi1 = expectation(pX, (self.kern, self.feature))\n        psi2 = tf.reduce_sum(expectation(pX, (self.kern, self.feature), (self.kern, self.feature)), axis=0)\n        Kuu = features.Kuu(self.feature, self.kern, jitter=settings.jitter)\n        L = tf.cholesky(Kuu)\n        sigma2 = self.likelihood.variance\n        sigma = tf.sqrt(sigma2)\n\n        # Compute intermediate matrices\n        A = tf.matrix_triangular_solve(L, tf.transpose(psi1), lower=True) / sigma\n        tmp = tf.matrix_triangular_solve(L, psi2, lower=True)\n        AAT = tf.matrix_triangular_solve(L, tf.transpose(tmp), lower=True) / sigma2\n        B = AAT + tf.eye(num_inducing, dtype=settings.float_type)\n        LB = tf.cholesky(B)\n        log_det_B = 2. * tf.reduce_sum(tf.log(tf.matrix_diag_part(LB)))\n        c = tf.matrix_triangular_solve(LB, tf.matmul(A, self.Y), lower=True) / sigma\n\n        # KL[q(x) || p(x)]\n        dX_var = self.X_var if len(self.X_var.get_shape()) == 2 else tf.matrix_diag_part(self.X_var)\n        NQ = tf.cast(tf.size(self.X_mean), settings.float_type)\n        D = tf.cast(tf.shape(self.Y)[1], settings.float_type)\n        KL = -0.5 * tf.reduce_sum(tf.log(dX_var)) \\\n             + 0.5 * tf.reduce_sum(tf.log(self.X_prior_var)) \\\n             - 0.5 * NQ \\\n             + 0.5 * tf.reduce_sum((tf.square(self.X_mean - self.X_prior_mean) + dX_var) / self.X_prior_var)\n\n        # {"prompt": "def checksum(sin):\n    \"\"\"\n    Determine validity of a Canadian Social Insurance Number.\n    Validation is performed using a modified Luhn Algorithm.  To check\n    the Every second digit of the SIN is doubled and the result is\n    summed.  If the result is a multiple of ten, the Social Insurance\n    Number is considered valid.\n\n    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Insurance_Number\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    # Remove spaces and dashes\n    sin = sin.replace(' ', '')\n    sin = sin.replace('-', '')\n\n    # Check length\n    if len(sin)!= 9:\n        return False\n\n    # Check sum\n    sum = 0\n    for i in range(0, 8):\n        if i % 2 == 0:\n            sum += int(sin[i])\n        else:\n            sum += int(sin[i]) * 2\n\n    if sum % 10!= 0:\n        return False\n\n    return True\n\n\ndef", "solution": "\n\n    # Remove spaces and create a list of digits.\n    checksumCollection = list(sin.replace(' ', ''))\n    checksumCollection = [int(i) for i in checksumCollection]\n\n    # Discard the last digit, we will be calculating it later.\n    checksumCollection[-1] = 0\n\n    # Iterate over the provided SIN and double every second digit.\n    # In the case that doubling that digit results in a two-digit\n    # number, then add the two digits together and keep that sum.\n\n    for i in range(1, len(checksumCollection), 2):\n        result = checksumCollection[i] * 2\n        if result < 10:\n            checksumCollection[i] = result\n        else:\n            checksumCollection[i] = result - 10 + 1\n\n    # The appropriate checksum digit is the value that, when summed\n    # with the first eight values, results in a value divisible by 10\n\n    check_digit = 10 - (sum(checksumCollection) % 10)\n    check_digit = (0 if check_digit == 10 else check_digit)\n\n    return check_digit"}

{"prompt": "def process_tokens(words, normalize_plurals=True):\n    \"\"\"Normalize cases and remove plurals.\n\n    Each word is represented by the most common case.\n    If a word appears with an \"s\" on the end and without an \"s\" on the end,\n    the version with \"s\" is assumed to be a plural and merged with the\n    version without \"s\" (except if the word ends with \"ss\").\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    words : iterable of strings\n        Words to count.\n\n    normalize_plurals : bool, default=True\n        Whether to try and detect plurals and remove trailing \"s\".\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    counts : dict from string to int\n        Counts for each unique word, with cases represented by the most common\n        case, and plurals removed.\n\n    standard_forms : dict from string to string\n        For each lower-case word the standard capitalization.\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\"s.\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    words : iterable of strings\n        Normalized words.\n    \"\"\"\n    words = [word.lower() for word in words]\n    if normalize_plurals:\n        words = [\n            word[:-1] if word.endswith(\"s\") and word[:-1] in words else word\n            for word in words\n        ]\n    return words\n\n\ndef", "solution": "\n    # words can be either a list of unigrams or bigrams\n    # d is a dict of dicts.\n    # Keys of d are word.lower().
